transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I just can’t seem to get a full night’s sleep anymore, my mind won’t let me rest and I wake up feeling exhausted. It has gotten to the point where I feel completely drained during the day and just can't function like I used to.
Have you been feeling sad, empty, or hopeless, or has your lack of sleep been affecting your mood in any way?

I don't really feel sad or hopeless, but the constant tension and lack of sleep have made me extremely irritable and on edge. I find myself snapping at my husband over trivial things like misplacing the remote, and both he and my choir director have noticed that I seem unusually tired and withdrawn lately. I feel terrible afterward because I know my family doesn't deserve that kind of reaction.
Have you been experiencing any recurring, persistent thoughts or worries that you can't seem to control, or feelings of fear or anxiety that are overwhelming to you?

Yes, my mind is constantly scanning for worst-case scenarios, like my mother's health failing or a work server crashing during a storm. Even when I tell myself to stop, the worries just keep looping and multiplying in my head. It gets to the point where I can't even focus on a Bible study or my crochet because these "what ifs" just keep barging in.
Can you tell me more about when these worries and 'what ifs' started, and if they seem to be triggered by specific events or situations, or if they are more constant and pervasive?

It all started building about a year ago when my mother's health crises began and I took on more caregiving on top of my IT job. While specific things like a missed call from her clinic or an email from my boss trigger these worst-case scenarios, the worry has become constant and pervasive. It just loops in my mind all day long, even during quiet moments when nothing is actually happening.

Can you describe how your worries and 'what ifs' relate to your daily life and responsibilities, and whether they seem to be focused on a specific domain, like your mother's health or your job, or if they are more generalized across all areas of your life?

My worries are definitely generalized and spread across all areas of my life rather than just one. My mind is constantly scanning for what could go wrong, from my mother's blood pressure and missed clinic calls to a server crashing at my IT job or even forgetting to pay a household bill. It feels like almost any small trigger sets off a chain of worst-case scenarios across all these different responsibilities.
Have you been avoiding any activities, situations, or responsibilities because of your worries or fears, or have you been trying to push through despite feeling overwhelmed?

I have actually pulled back from activities I used to enjoy, like my Saturday walking club and church events, because I feel too drained and distracted to participate. At work, I am trying to push through my responsibilities, but I struggle to focus and find myself having to reread the same network reports over and over.

Can you tell me more about what specifically makes you want to avoid those activities you used to enjoy, is it the fear of something going wrong or the feeling of being overwhelmed that's holding you back?

It is actually a mix of both. I feel too physically and mentally drained from the lack of sleep to participate in my walking group, but when I do try to relax with crochet or Bible study, my mind is constantly interrupted by "what if" worries. My body also feels so tense and wound up, as if I am bracing for an emergency call, that I just can't relax and enjoy them.
Have you experienced any episodes of intense fear or discomfort that reach a peak within minutes, accompanied by symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shortness of breath?

No, I haven't experienced those kinds of sudden, intense episodes of panic or physical symptoms like a racing heart or shortness of breath. Instead, my anxiety feels more like a constant, steady level of tension and worry that stays with me throughout the entire day.

You've described a constant and pervasive worry that affects many areas of your life, but can you tell me if there are any specific times or situations when these worries seem to significantly increase or decrease in intensity?

My worries definitely spike at night, usually between 11 PM and 1 or 2 AM when I'm trying to sleep, as well as when I get sudden triggers like an email from my boss or a missed call from my mom's clinic. On the other hand, there aren't really times when the worry decreases. Even when I try to relax with my crochet or go for a walk, my mind and body remain completely wound tight and unable to rest.
Can you think of any situations or activities that you have not avoided, where you feel somewhat able to manage your worries and function without significant distress?

Honestly, it feels like there are almost no activities right now where I can escape the worry and function without distress. Even my favorite relaxing outlets, like crocheting, Bible study, or walks with my group, are constantly interrupted by looping "what-if" thoughts and a physical feeling of being wound tight. It has just become incredibly difficult to find any moments that are truly peaceful.

You mentioned avoiding some activities due to feeling drained and distracted, but are there any situations or tasks that you feel you cannot avoid, such as work or caregiving for your mother, and if so, how do you manage your worries in those contexts?

I absolutely cannot avoid my job managing the city's network or my caregiving duties for my mother, so I try to manage by tightly scheduling every hour of my day and telling myself to stop worrying. Unfortunately, it doesn't actually work; I still find myself constantly wound tight, bracing for an emergency, and having to reread network reports multiple times because my focus is so fractured by looping "what-if" scenarios.
Can you describe if there are any specific themes or patterns to your worries, such as always focusing on potential dangers or always expecting the worst outcome in various situations?

Yes, my mind is constantly scanning for potential dangers and immediately jumps to the absolute worst-case scenarios. Even minor triggers, like a missed call from my mom's clinic or an email from my boss, set off a chain reaction where I'm suddenly imagining her falling in the bathroom or a major city server crashing during a storm.

Can you tell me if you have experienced any significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning due to your worries, and if so, can you give me some specific examples?

Yes, my worries and lack of sleep are definitely impacting my work and social life. At my job, I've started having to reread the same network reports because I simply can't stay focused. Socially, I've had to pull back from my church activities and Saturday walking club because I feel far too drained and distracted to participate.

Do you feel that your worries and anxiety symptoms are directly related to your mother's health issues and your increased caregiving responsibilities, or do they seem to be more excessive and pervasive, extending far beyond these specific stressors?

While my mother's health crises definitely triggered this intense stress, my worries have become much more pervasive and extend far beyond just her. My mind is constantly scanning for any potential disaster, whether it's worrying about a city server crashing during a storm, forgetting to pay a household bill, or getting anxious over a simple email from my boss. It really feels like my anxiety has branched out into every single area of my life.

Can you describe how your excessive worry and anxiety symptoms have affected your daily life and relationships over the past year, and whether you feel like you're able to cope with these stressors or if they're becoming overwhelming?

It has become completely overwhelming and I feel unable to cope; over the past year, this constant worry has forced me to pull back from church and my walking club, and I struggle to even focus on my IT reports. It's also hurting my relationships because I'm so irritable and snap at my husband over small things. No matter how much I tell myself to stop, the thoughts just loop uncontrollably and leave me feeling constantly wound tight.

Do you feel that your excessive worry and anxiety are primarily in response to your mother's health issues and caregiving responsibilities, or have they become a more general pattern of responding to stressors in your life?

While my mother's health crises certainly started all of this, it has definitely become a more general pattern of worrying. I now find myself constantly scanning for worst-case scenarios across all areas of my life, like work server crashes or missing a household bill. It feels like my mind is just always on high alert for what could go wrong next.

Can you clarify if your worries and anxiety symptoms are more focused on specific, identifiable threats or stressors, such as your mother's health or work issues, or if they are more free-floating and unrelated to any specific situation or event?

While my worries definitely started with specific things like my mother's health and my job, it now feels like the anxiety has spread and become much more free-floating. My mind is constantly scanning for anything that could go wrong, so even small, everyday things like a missed call or a routine email can trigger a spiral of worst-case scenarios. It has reached a point where the worry feels constant and incredibly hard to turn off, regardless of the situation.
Do you feel like your worries are primarily driven by a fear of the unknown or unexpected events, or are they more focused on specific outcomes or consequences that you're trying to prevent?

It feels like a combination of both, but it is primarily driven by an intense need to prevent specific bad outcomes. I constantly run through contingency plans in my head to prevent disasters, like a city server crashing or my mother falling in the bathroom. At the same time, I have this persistent, tense dread of unexpected emergencies—like a sudden phone call or a missed email—catching me completely off guard.
Do you often find yourself repeatedly going over plans or mentally rehearsing scenarios in an attempt to prepare for potential problems or prevent them from happening?

Yes, I do this constantly. When I lie awake at night, my mind is endlessly running through backup plans for the city's network or imagining worst-case scenarios like my mother falling in the bathroom. I feel like I have to tightly schedule every hour of my day to prevent things from slipping through the cracks, and even a missed call or email sets off a whole chain of worrying about what could go wrong.
Can you estimate how many hours a day you spend worrying or engaging in mental rehearsals of potential problems, and are there any times when you're able to completely stop this worrying?

It is hard to give a specific number of hours because the worrying feels almost constant throughout the day and night, as my mind is always scanning for problems with my mom or my work. I am never able to completely stop it; even when I tell myself to stop or try to relax with my crochet or Bible study, the worries just keep looping and interrupting me every few minutes.

Can you tell me if you've experienced any significant changes in your physical health, such as headaches, muscle tension, or fatigue, that seem to be directly related to your worrying and anxiety symptoms?

Yes, I have been dealing with a lot of muscle tension and fatigue. My body constantly feels wound tight, as if I am bracing for an emergency call, which makes it impossible to relax. Because of my poor sleep, I wake up feeling completely exhausted and drained every single day.
Are there any specific situations or activities that you avoid because you fear they might trigger or worsen your anxiety, and if so, can you describe them?

I don't really avoid activities out of fear of triggering my anxiety itself. Instead, I've pulled back from things I used to enjoy—like my Saturday walking club, church activities, and crocheting—because I feel too exhausted and distracted to focus. My body also feels too tense and constantly 'on standby' for an emergency to actually sit still and enjoy them.
Can you think of any activities or situations that you still manage to participate in without significant anxiety or worry, despite feeling drained and distracted?

Unfortunately, it feels like almost no activity is free from the worry and tension anymore. Even simple hobbies I used to enjoy, like crocheting, watching TV, or Bible study, are constantly interrupted by intrusive "what-if" thoughts. I've actually had to pull back from my walking club and church activities because I just feel too drained and distracted to engage in them without anxiety.
Can you think of any specific situations or events that trigger your worries and anxiety, and are there any common themes among these triggers?

The two main themes are my mother's health and caregiving, and my demanding job in municipal network security and disaster recovery. Specific triggers like getting a missed call from her medical clinic, an email from my boss, or worrying about a server crashing during a storm instantly set off worst-case scenarios in my mind. It just feels like I am always bracing for some kind of disaster in those two areas.
Have you experienced any changes in your appetite or weight over the past year, and if so, can you describe them?

I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my appetite or weight over the past year. My main struggles have definitely been with my lack of sleep, the constant worrying, and feeling so wound up all the time.
Can you tell me if you have ever experienced a period of at least six months where you did not struggle with excessive worry or anxiety about everyday things?

Yes, absolutely. Before my mother's health crises began about a year ago, I did not experience this kind of constant, excessive worry or anxiety at all. For many years before that, I was able to manage my work and daily life without any of these struggles.
